This application under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (CrPC) is filed seeking quash of FIR in Crime No. 11210045201954 of 2020, registered with Pandesara Police Station, Surat City for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506(2) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and the Charge-sheet in C.C. No.
23009 of 2020 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No. 27, Surat.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14959/2020 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined 2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No. 27, Surat
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the second respondent, who is the de facto complainant and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.

1 3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the time of hearing the application, the learned counsel for the applicant as well as the learned counsel for the second respondent - de facto complainant would submit that both the parties have entered into compromise and they have settled all the disputes between them and they have decided to compound the offence.
The learned counsel for the applicant has also filed the affidavit of the second respondent - de facto complainant to this effect.
4. The de facto complainant is physically present before the Court today.

When questioned, she has unequivocally stated that she has entered into compromise with the accused and squared up all the disputes between them and the litigation pending in various Courts and that, a sum of Rs.24 lakh was deposited before the learned Family Court, Vadodara by way of a Demand Draft and Rs.1,51,000/- was paid to her.
She also stated that she has no objection to quash the FIR and the criminal proceedings initiated thereon.

5. Although, the offences for which the FIR was registered are of non-compoundable offences, as per the dictum laid down by the Apex Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303,
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14959/2020 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined in appropriate cases, where the offences have not impact on the society, the Court, in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (CrPC), can permit the parties to compound the offences even which are non- compoundable.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, some cases are exempted which are catelogued in the said judgment of the Apex Court, the present case is not falling within the said exempted cases.

6. Therefore, permission is accorded to the applicant and the de facto complainant to compound the offence as prayed for and the compromise is recorded.
7.
Resultantly, the application is allowed in terms of the compromise.

The FIR in Crime No.
11210045201954 of 2020, registered with Pandesara Police Station, Surat City for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506(2) of the IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and the Charge-sheet in C.C. No. 23009 of 2020 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No. 27, Surat, against the applicant, are hereby quashed against the applicant.
